catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extracted from Continuous Architecture System (CAS) runner codebase, governance lifecycle engines, LLM abstractions, and steering projection models.
analysis_limits: Repository inspection limited to manifest dependencies, directory tree, and key file signatures in src/cas_runner and cas-knowledge.

system_map.overview: CAS (Continuous Architecture System) runner provides an agentic governance orchestration engine that maps, evaluates, merges, and projects architectural capabilities and governance policies into automated workflows via LLM integrations and deterministic state transitions.

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Reconciles and resolves concurrent architectural decisions, governance state mutations, and steering block configurations across projects.

agents.name: ComplianceEngine
agents.role: Evaluates architectural deliverables and Git deltas against codified organizational rules, generating compliance findings and metrics.

agents.name: GovernanceActionEngine
agents.role: Executes state transition sequences across the architectural artifact lifecycle according to an explicit transition registry.

orchestration.description: Orchestration is coordinated by FlowRunner, which sequentially executes discrete governance, steering, and evaluation steps while managing shared execution context and propagating state across runs.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provides unified access to downstream LLM provider backends through litellm.

tools_and_integrations.name: OpenTelemetrySDK
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Collects distributed traces and traceable governance metrics during agent flow execution.

tools_and_integrations.name: MockLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Enables deterministic offline evaluation and testing of governance flows without external network calls.

state_and_memory.description: File-based architectural knowledge repository containing decisions, governance rules, models, patterns, and runtime evaluation records.
Steering runtime index composed of structured facts and capability lineage derived from Git deltas and architectural manifests.
Contextual execution state, metric traces, and transient finding objects generated during an orchestration run.

patterns.name: Pluggable LLM Provider Abstraction

tool_protocols.notes: Encapsulates model invocation via litellm unified client.

optimisation_targets.notes: Decouples business logic from upstream LLM provider API changes.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Direct unified client interface reduces operational overhead across agents.

patterns.summary: Wraps LLM invocations in a standardized client interface enabling transparent switching between production multi-provider models and deterministic test mock clients.
patterns.intent: Decouple orchestration and governance agents from provider-specific APIs while facilitating deterministic local testing.
patterns.context: Agentic components (merger, compliance engine) require model completions but must remain agnostic to specific LLM endpoints and testable without active API keys.
forces: Need multi-model flexibility across distinct providers without changing prompt consumption logic.
Requirement to test agent pipelines offline in CI without consuming API budget.
patterns.solution: Define interchangeable LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient classes offering a uniform completion interface across all governance operations.
implementation_signals: MockLLMClient offering pre-configured responses for unit and integration pipelines.

benefits: Enables transparent model swaps without refactoring agent decision code.
Allows deterministic offline verification of agent pipelines in CI.
costs: Abstracts away provider-specific features unless explicitly mapped.
Requires mock synchronisation whenever agent output contracts change.
failure_modes: Mock client behavior diverging from real LLM schema generation characteristics.

patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse LiteLLMClient pattern in multi-model architectures to avoid coupling agent logic to single-vendor APIs.

patterns.name: Registry-Guarded Governance State Machine

tool_protocols.notes: State transitions are managed through programmatic code contracts rather than tool calling.

optimisation_targets.notes: Strict validation prevents invalid artifact lifecycle mutations.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Deterministic guardrails constrain autonomous agent changes.

patterns.summary: Constrains autonomous actions and artifact state progressions through an explicit transition registry that validates preconditions before allowing state shifts.
patterns.intent: Prevent LLM or autonomous workers from promoting or transitioning architectural artifacts into invalid states.
patterns.context: Architectural artifacts (patterns, rules, decisions) must adhere to defined lifecycles (e.g. exploring -> validating -> stable) and cannot skip governance checks.
forces: Autonomous agents must execute actions while preventing unauthorized or invalid state transitions.
Traceability of state transitions must be retained for audits.
patterns.solution: Route all state changes through GovernanceActionEngine, which validates requested actions against TransitionRegistry before applying mutations.
implementation_signals: TransitionRegistry class defining permissible state transitions.
GovernanceActionEngine mediating execution and rejecting illegal operations.

evidence.note: Registry and execution engine enforcing state lifecycle transitions
Action descriptors and domain exception types for illegal actions

benefits: Centralizes authorization and transition rules into a single verifiable registry.
costs: All new artifact lifecycles require explicit registry configuration.
Requires strict error-handling wrappers around agent-initiated transitions.
failure_modes: Unmapped state transitions causing agent task failure cascades.

patterns.reuse_notes: Implement whenever agent actions mutate business-critical or compliance-tracked records.

patterns.name: Structured Fact Projection Indexing

tool_protocols.notes: Facts are projected directly into model prompt contexts as typed data structures.

optimisation_targets.notes: Injects only validated, structured facts into prompts to reduce token usage and hallucination.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Pre-structured context projection avoids unpredictable vector RAG hallucination.

patterns.summary: Extracts and indexes typed capability facts and architectural deltas from repository history, projecting them into prompt-ready structured contexts for agent reasoning.
patterns.intent: Supply agents with factual, verifiable context without flooding prompts with unstructured data or ungrounded knowledge.
patterns.context: Agents analyzing git changes and governance compliance require precise context regarding capability lineages and repository deltas.
forces: LLMs hallucinate context when provided ambiguous or unstructured raw git dumps.
Prompt token budgets require concise, relevant summaries of current system architecture.
patterns.solution: Index system capability sets into a SteeringRuntimeIndex containing typed PromptFact and CapabilityRecord models derived from RawGitDelta and CapabilityLineage.
implementation_signals: SteeringRuntimeIndex compiling capability sets and facts.
PromptFact model structuring key-value facts for prompt synthesis.

evidence.note: Typed models defining fact indexing and runtime projection

benefits: Drastically reduces prompt hallucinations by grounding agent context in verified facts.
Enables selective prompt context assembly based on affected capability categories.
costs: Requires maintenance of extraction parsers for capability records.
Schema changes to facts require synchronization across prompt templates.
failure_modes: Omission of critical git deltas during index creation leading to blind spots during compliance checks.

patterns.reuse_notes: Adapt this pattern for code-generation or code-review agents requiring precise historical knowledge of codebase capabilities.

patterns.name: Sequential Flow Orchestration Pipeline

tool_protocols.notes: Steps run through a deterministically scheduled runner loop.

optimisation_targets.notes: Sequential execution guarantees dependency satisfaction across stages.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: A single centralized flow runner prevents race conditions in governance evaluation.

patterns.summary: Coordinates multistep architectural governance and compliance execution through a centralized sequential pipeline passing shared context between stages.
patterns.intent: Ensure deterministic ordering and dependency propagation across initialization, analysis, evaluation, and publishing stages.
patterns.context: Continuous architecture analysis involves multi-stage tasks (bootstrap, lint/validation, LLM evaluation, report generation) where downstream steps rely on upstream outputs.
forces: Uncoordinated multi-agent parallel execution can cause race conditions on file-based state.
Failures in early validation steps must immediately short-circuit expensive LLM operations.
patterns.solution: FlowRunner coordinates discrete stages sequentially, passing an execution context that accumulates intermediate results and short-circuits on critical failures.
implementation_signals: FlowRunner class orchestrating ordered execution phases.
CLI entry point invoking FlowRunner with explicit configuration flags.

evidence.note: Centralized execution runner managing stage lifecycles
CLI driver delegating arguments to FlowRunner

benefits: Predictable execution path with unambiguous error boundaries.
Early termination saves model API consumption when preliminary validation fails.
costs: Execution time scales linearly with the number of sequential stages.
Limited ability to exploit parallelism across independent checks.
failure_modes: Cascading pipeline failure when an upstream non-critical step throws an unhandled exception.

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard pattern for workflow-driven agent systems requiring deterministic verification gates prior to agentic generation.

patterns.name: Agentic Reconciliation Merger

tool_protocols.notes: Uses LLM reasoning to merge disparate architectural blocks into unified definitions.

optimisation_targets.notes: Preserves architectural integrity when merging multi-project governance blocks.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Autonomous conflict resolution bounded by schema validation.

patterns.summary: Employs an LLM-assisted reconciliation agent to analyze semantic conflicts across governance configurations and produce a unified, resolved state.
patterns.intent: Resolve semantic divergences in governance blocks that standard git or text-based line mergers cannot intelligently resolve.
patterns.context: Multiple project repositories generate localized governance configurations or rules that need to be harmonized into the global cas-knowledge base.
forces: Mechanical text merging produces syntactically valid but semantically conflicting architecture rules.
Manual human reconciliation of rule changes across multiple projects creates operational bottlenecks.
patterns.solution: AgenticMerger ingests overlapping governance blocks, prompts the model for semantic alignment, and generates a structured ResolutionResult.
implementation_signals: AgenticMerger class encapsulating LLM-driven reconciliation logic.
ResolutionResult model returning resolved contents and conflict resolution metadata.

evidence.note: Core class orchestrating LLM-based governance reconciliation
Structured contract capturing merged output and resolution details

benefits: Resolves nuanced conceptual overlaps in governance rules and steering configurations.
Captures structured rationales explaining how conflict resolutions were derived.
costs: Requires model tokens for comparison tasks.
Must be coupled with validation checks to verify the synthesized block remains valid schema.
failure_modes: Subtle drift where the LLM reconciler drops nuanced edge-case constraints during synthesis.

patterns.reuse_notes: Use this pattern when merging competing pull-request documents, policy definitions, or agent outputs containing semantic overlaps.

patterns.name: Rule-Grounded Compliance Evaluation

tool_protocols.notes: Applies programmatic and model-guided evaluations to git changes.

optimisation_targets.notes: Automates architecture review without human reviewer delays.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Automated evaluation yields explicit findings for human or downstream pipeline action.

patterns.summary: Evaluates code and architectural delta compliance by evaluating diffs against codified rule contexts and generating structured finding metrics.
patterns.intent: Continuously verify whether repository changes conform to organizational architectural standards before PR merge.
patterns.context: Within CI workflows (e.g. cas-build-validation.yml), PRs must be audited against cas-knowledge architectural rules.
forces: Human architectural reviews are infrequent and slow down deployment velocity.
Purely static linting tools cannot evaluate architectural intent or semantic compliance.
patterns.solution: ComplianceEngine consumes RawGitDelta and rule context files, evaluating violations and returning structured ComplianceFinding and ComplianceMetrics instances.
implementation_signals: ComplianceFinding and ComplianceMetrics Pydantic models containing structured evaluation records.

evidence.note: Evaluator applying rules to codebase deltas
Data contracts for individual violations and composite scores

benefits: Transforms abstract architectural guidelines into automated, actionable feedback.
Yields quantifiable metrics on compliance health over time.
costs: Rules must be maintained in structured formats within cas-knowledge.
Potential for false-positive findings if rule descriptions are ambiguous.
failure_modes: Rules misinterpreting code context resulting in noisy compliance rejections.

patterns.reuse_notes: Deploy in CI/CD pipelines to enforce domain-driven design or architectural boundary constraints.

patterns.name: Traceable Metric Telemetry Envelope

tool_protocols.notes: Uses OpenTelemetry standard integration for agent tracing.

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees observability and auditability across all agent governance decisions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Standard telemetry envelopes preserve traceability without altering decision logic.

patterns.summary: Envelopes agent evaluation outputs, health scores, and throughput in traceable metric models backed by OpenTelemetry spans to guarantee auditability.
patterns.intent: Maintain continuous traceability for agentic decisions, compliance calculations, and governance state shifts.
patterns.context: Agent decisions in autonomous governance must be verifiable by human auditors and linked to concrete execution traces.
forces: Autonomous agent decisions without traceability create operational opacity and regulatory risk.
Diagnostic debugging of complex agent runs requires linked metadata.
patterns.solution: Wrap evaluation results and governance health calculations into TraceableMetric models and trace spans stored under cas-knowledge/runtime/traces.
implementation_signals: TraceableMetric model attaching timestamps, run IDs, and trace IDs to metric values.

evidence.note: Models embedding traceability envelopes for metrics
opentelemetry-api and opentelemetry-sdk declared as core runtime dependencies

benefits: Complete provenance trail connecting code deltas to agent evaluation scores.
Seamless export to enterprise APM and tracing backends via OpenTelemetry.
costs: Small serialization and runtime memory overhead.
Trace store retention must be managed to prevent disk bloat.
failure_modes: Uncorrelated traces if run identifiers are dropped during sub-task execution.

patterns.reuse_notes: Essential pattern for enterprise AI agents operating in regulated or compliance-critical environments.

patterns.name: Steering Block Workspace Bootstrapping

tool_protocols.notes: Injects codified steering configurations into repository agent contexts.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures developer IDE agents and CI runners inherit consistent steering rules.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Static configuration injection avoids dynamic agent drift.

patterns.summary: Injects standardized governance and architectural steering prompt blocks into target workspaces during environment bootstrap to ground external developer agents.
patterns.intent: Ensure that localized AI tools (such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI) adhere to system architecture guidelines from project initialization.
patterns.context: External coding assistants in developer workspaces lack awareness of project-specific architecture rules unless explicitly prompted.
forces: Developers forget to feed architectural guidelines into their localized AI coding prompts.
Manual copying of prompt guidelines leads to divergence across repositories.
patterns.solution: Use bootstrap routines to merge a standardized CAS governance steering block directly into repo instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md).
implementation_signals: merge_cas_governance_block function synchronizing markdown configuration blocks.
init_workspace and bootstrap routines initializing steering contexts.

evidence.note: Logic inserting and updating CAS steering blocks into workspace agent files
Workspace agent guidelines file managed by CAS steering

benefits: Zero-friction propagation of enterprise architectural standards to local IDE agents.
Prevents divergence of agent steering rules between developer environments and CI.
costs: Can overwrite custom developer configurations if delimiter markers are improperly parsed.
Adds boilerplate instructions to workspace instruction files.
failure_modes: Malformed delimiters causing duplicate steering blocks or corruption in markdown instruction files.

patterns.reuse_notes: Use this heuristic to keep multi-agent and local-assistant prompt files aligned with centralized organizational policies.

anti_patterns.name: Unbounded Semantic Merge Promotion
symptoms: AgenticMerger resolving conflicting governance blocks directly into production files without deterministic schema re-validation.
Accepting LLM synthesized configurations without secondary transition registry checks.

where_observed.note: Potential risk if merged outputs bypass TransitionRegistry or validation schemas

impact: Silent drift in architectural rules where the model introduces plausible but invalid governance invariants.
Erosion of regulatory guarantees over time.
suggested_remediation: Subject all AgenticMerger outputs to strict Pydantic/jsonschema schema validation and require explicit TransitionRegistry gate approval before persisting merged blocks.

anti_patterns.name: Unfiltered Git Delta Prompt Flooding
symptoms: Passing raw git diffs containing lockfiles, compiled assets, or large binary changes directly into agent prompt contexts.
Model latency spikes and context window exhaustion during compliance checks.

where_observed.note: Handling raw git deltas before distillation into PromptFact

impact: High token expenditures and degraded reasoning fidelity due to prompt dilution.
Frequent API rate limit or context length truncation errors.
suggested_remediation: Filter and distill RawGitDelta objects into CapabilityRecord and PromptFact summaries before invoking LLM analysis.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Formalized via typed Pydantic models (PromptFact, ResolutionResult, ComplianceFinding) that parse and validate all inputs to and outputs from LLM invocations.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Enforces strict interface contracts between unstructured LLM outputs and downstream software components.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Integrated OpenTelemetry telemetry wrappers and traceable metric records to correlate individual agent operations with overall system health.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Ensures end-to-end auditability of automated architectural decisions across enterprise projects.

open_questions.question: How are long-term historical evaluations in cas-knowledge/runtime/evaluations pruned or compacted?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Unchecked accumulation of JSON evaluation logs in git repositories can bloat repository size and degrade clone performance.
open_questions.evidence_gap: The files under cas-knowledge/runtime/ demonstrate evaluation recording, but no automated retention policy or compaction script is evident in cas_runner.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Inspect GitHub Actions workflows (cas-continuous-architecture.yml) for repository cleanup or archival jobs.
